name: LocustDB
tagline: Experimental Rust columnar analytics engine built to scan billions of rows per second on one machine.
description: LocustDB is Clemens Winter's experimental analytics database, begun at Dropbox in 2017 and continued as a personal open-source project. It ingests CSV or its own storage format into compressed, partitioned columns and runs a SQL subset (filters, aggregations, group by, order by, LIKE; no joins) through a vectorized, massively parallel query engine; the author's write-ups showed billions of records per second scanned on a single desktop. Data is append-only and can only be deleted or expired in bulk; recent 0.5 versions add durable on-disk storage with a write-ahead log, faster compaction and pcodec float compression. It is a single-developer research system: fast and instructive, but not production infrastructure.
statusNote: Experimental single-developer project; last release 0.5.6 (Apr 2025) and last main-branch commit July 2025.

scale.notes: Single machine; all cores are used per query. Data must fit the partition and memory limits configured.

strengths: Vectorized, parallel execution that saturates all cores of one machine
Aggressive per-column compression (dictionary, delta, lz4, pcodec)
Fast ingestion of CSV and append-only data
Clean Rust codebase worth reading for query-engine design
weaknesses: Experimental and maintained by one person
No joins, updates or transactions; append-only data
useCases: Ad-hoc analytics over large CSV or log datasets on one box
Exploring large append-only event or metric tables
notIdealFor: Production analytics needing joins or SLAs
